title: Many heads
summary: The head gallery, naming heads, and ablating one to see what it does.

steps.text: Each layer runs several heads side by side, each with its own query, key and value projections, so each can learn a different habit. The **head gallery** shows them all for this prompt.
steps.prompt: Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She

steps.text: The badge under each head summarises its habit: a fixed target (previous, self, first) if it has one; otherwise how **sharp** it is and how far back it looks on average.

ask.question: Click the **sharpest** head in the gallery: the one that puts most weight on a single key.
ask.hint: Look for the thinnest diagonal lines, and a “sharp” badge.
ask.correct: Give it a name in the box under it, if you can describe what it does.

steps.text: To learn what a head does, remove it. Ablating zeroes its output in every trace. Use the **ablate** button under the head you picked, then open the **interventions** tab to see the effect on the loss and on each position's prediction.
Heads that matter raise the loss when removed, and the per-position chart shows where they matter. Try a few heads: some barely change anything.
